result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that the three numbers don't show the program worked, and both offer real job measures with check-in points. A is more proportionate: it has a short plan, a clean script for the director and a sensible 'ask why' step. It also frames the quiz as short-term recall measured against later application, though its line on the survey ('flags dissatisfaction') is oddly worded and it never says that 12 agents is a small sample. B is more thorough on sample size and survey bias, but its director script says 'the content is landing' and that the program 'is working on learning', which contradicts its own point that the quiz has no baseline, and its list of measures is heavier than a small team needs. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the numbers don't show improved job performance, and both give the director wording with a date. B is more proportionate: one existing metric checked at 30 and 60 days, a comparison group and ticket spot checks. It also names the quiz as short-term recall. A is more honest about the small sample, but it overclaims that the program 'is working on learning', proposes a longer, more research-like list, and its knowledge check only runs at the start and end of the course. B's line on the survey ('This flags dissatisfaction') is garbled, and it never mentions the small sample size.
